newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close higher despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close higher despite profit-taking.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Wednesday despite the fact that impressive early gains were sharply reduced by profit-taking, with dealers seeing advances again on Thursday.

"Forecasts of new records inspired by U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony proved not to hold. Profit-taking and technical resistance hit early gains sharply just before the index neared last week's record 195.61," one dealer said.
"We should have held on to more of the early Greenspan- inspired advances. The market undertone is positive and Wall Street and the dollar look good, so I see more gains," he added.
The KFX top-20 index gained 1.07 point or 0.56 percent to end the day at 191.66, after peaking at 195.40.
Overall bourse turnover was 1.249 billion crowns. The KFX August future rose 3.20 point to 194.00 with 604 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

SAS was the day's most traded paper with 445,000 shares changing hands. Boosted by buy recommendations, the SAS share, which has been much in focus in recent days, closed 3.5 crowns up at 106, almost 50 percent higher than just six weeks ago.
